props.text:
# Three ways to wear the trench this autumn

_AnyCompany Apparel Journal · editorial · 2026-09-14_

The trench coat is the one piece that survives every edit of the Utility line. Ours is cut
double breasted and knee length in a plain, stone-coloured cotton gabardine, with a wide
notched lapel, a buttoned storm flap and a belt that you should actually tie rather than
buckle.

**One.** Over straight-leg, high-waist jeans and a plain white crew-neck t-shirt. Roll the
jeans once so the ankle boots show; the boots are lace-up, brown leather, with a
rubber sole that copes with wet pavements.

**Two.** Over a midi shirt dress in the same stone tone, collar open, sleeves pushed to the
elbow. The coat stays unbelted and hangs straight: an easy, loose silhouette that works for
the office and the train home.

**Three.** Belted tight over a fine turtleneck sweater and wide-leg trousers with a pressed
crease. Add a herringbone wool scarf and a structured leather tote. This is the version we
photographed for the season campaign.

Whatever the version, the trench's patch pockets are deep enough for a paperback, and the
regular fit leaves room for a sweater underneath without pulling at the shoulders.

props.text:
# Last of the summer light

_AnyCompany Apparel · social post · 2026-09-02_

Last of the summer light and the floral a-line midi dress is doing all the work. V-neck,
short puff sleeves, a normal waist that sits exactly where it should, and a print that
photographs better than it has any right to.

We paired it with knee-high boots in black leather (zip-up on the inside, a low block heel)
and a small crossbody bag with a metal chain strap. Tights optional; the boots do most of
the warming.

Styling note from the studio: keep everything else plain. One floral, one texture (the
leather), one metal. That is the whole formula.

props.text:
# Fitting-room notes: the Evening tuxedo

_AnyCompany Apparel fitting-room notes · product · 2026-08-27_

The satin-lapel tuxedo jacket is single breasted with one button and a peak lapel faced in
black satin. Fit is tight through the chest and regular through the waist; the sleeves are
wrist-length and finished with four working buttons. The jacket is fully lined, hip length,
in a plain black wool.

The satin-stripe tuxedo trousers are cut straight with a high waist and a fly opening; the
side stripe matches the lapel facing. They are meant to sit on the shoe with a single
break, so ask for the hem to be pinned rather than guessed.

Under the jacket: a white dress shirt with a shirt collar and a plain front (no pleats), and
the slim silk tie in black. If the invitation says black tie, swap the tie for a bow tie and
add the velvet evening cape for the walk from the car.

Shoes: the patent leather loafer, no opening, worn with sheer black socks. A slim dress watch
in gold-toned steel and nothing else on the wrist.
